'''Nikolai Dmitrievich Brashman''' ({{langx|ru|Никола́й Дми́триевич Брáшман}}; {{langx|de|Nikolaus Braschmann}}; June 14, 1796 &ndash; {{Gregorian to Julian|25 May 1866}}) was a Russian [[mathematician]] of [[Jewish-Austrian]] origin.<ref name="mactutor">{{MacTutor Biography|id=Brashman}}</ref> He was a student of [[Joseph Johann Littrow]], and the advisor of [[Pafnuty Chebyshev]] and [[August Davidov]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=12541}}</ref>

He was born in Neu-Raußnitz (today [[Rousínov]] in [[Czech Republic]], then in [[Austrian Empire]]) and studied at the [[University of Vienna]] and [[Vienna University of Technology|Vienna Polytechnic Institute]]. In 1824 he moved to [[Saint Petersburg]] and then accepted a position at the [[Kazan State University|Kazan University]]. In 1834 he became a professor of applied mathematics at the [[Moscow State University|Moscow University]]. There he is best remembered as a founder of the [[Moscow Mathematical Society]] and its journal ''[[Matematicheskii Sbornik]]''.<ref>{{citation|title=The History of Approximation Theory: From Euler to Bernstein|first=Karl-Georg|last=Steffens|publisher=Springer|year=2007|isbn=9780817644758|page=22|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IjFJNoq638kC&pg=PA22}}.</ref>

For his mechanics textbook, in 1836 Brashman was awarded the [[Demidov Prize]] by the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]. The academy elected him a corresponding member in 1855. He died in [[Moscow]] in 1866.
